cards.title: Steady-State and Sparse Sampling Assumptions in NCA
cards.claim: Non-compartmental analysis (NCA) models for steady-state data assume equal dosing intervals (Tau) and that data is from a 'final' dose at steady state. These models support both rich and sparsely-sampled datasets (e.g., toxicokinetics).
conditions: Applicable when deriving exposure metrics from sparse or rich data for simulation validation or input.
Requires explicit definition of Tau for steady-state calculations.
required_inputs: Infusion duration for constant infusion models.
limitations: Assumes steady state has been reached; does not model accumulation dynamics directly.
Sparse sampling may limit the resolution of terminal slope estimation.
cards.downstream_use: Provides exposure metrics (AUC, Cmax) for comparison with simulated profiles or as inputs for PD modeling.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
